notes: Asserts the row's full arc inside ONE codex session and ONE turn: ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready, with the FIRST waiting episode raised by a command that writes (echo GATE-OK > gate.txt) and the SECOND by one that only reads (cat gate.txt). NOT known_failing: codex is structurally immune to #1861. irrlicht installs codex's PermissionRequest and PostToolUse hooks with hookMatcher = ".*" (core/adapters/inbound/agents/codex/hookinstaller.go), not with claudecode's nine-alternative tool-name allowlist, and HandlePermissionHook resolves the hook by EVENT name through session.HookSignal without ever reading a tool name -- so state_classifier rule 0 (permission_prompt -> waiting) fires for the read-only gate exactly as it does for the mutating one. On the agent side the gate is decided per COMMAND, not per tool: exec_policy.rs's render_decision_for_unmatched_command returns Decision::Prompt unconditionally under AskForApproval::UnlessTrusted ("Projects marked untrusted require approval for every command that is not explicitly allowed by an exec policy rule"), and codex has no read-only tool at all -- reads and writes both go through the exec tool, reaching the hook with the same tool_name "Bash" (HookToolName::bash()). WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE CLAIM: a green here proves the row's acceptance criteria (a read-only call's gate produces its own user-visible waiting episode, not skipped and not merged) but does NOT prove tool-class discrimination the way the claudecode sibling does -- there is no per-tool-name allowlist on codex for a read-only tool to fall out of. PRESESSION ADAPTER: the birth is two phases. A transient proc-<PID> row appears first and never goes working; the rollout session reconciles with a DIFFERENT session_id, and every post-birth phase anchors to that real session. The waiting->working between the two episodes is carried by PostToolUse (also matcher ".*"), which clears the permission-pending overlay once each approved command runs; the final ready is carried by Stop. NO CYCLE COUNT IS PINNED beyond the two episodes the scenario itself names as its subject. model is left unpinned for record to fill from the recording -- this host's config default is gpt-5.6-sol while the existing codex goldens pin gpt-5.5, and pinning either from here would fail every recording until corrected.

MUTATING half: the command that writes gate.txt opens codex's blocking approval overlay; the PermissionRequest hook (tool_name "Bash", or "apply_patch" if the model patches instead) sets PermissionPending -> rule 0 -> working -> waiting. This is the half 2-19 already covers; it is here so one recording can compare the two calls.

The user answers the first overlay with the preselected one-time option; the write runs and PostToolUse clears the pending overlay -> waiting -> working. The episode ends on the ANSWER, not on the turn.

THE ASSERTION UNDER TEST. The call that only reads (cat gate.txt) is gated too -- exec_policy.rs prompts for every unmatched command under -a untrusted, with no read-only exemption -- and must produce its OWN, second waiting episode: not skipped, and not merged into the mutating call's episode.
The user answers the read-only overlay; the read runs and PostToolUse clears the overlay -> waiting -> working
Stop fires at true turn end -> ready. The session does not remain waiting after the last overlay closes.
Trailing idle: the session stays ready for >=10s after the last overlay, catching a session left pinned at, or falling back to, waiting.
